subject: math
title: Place Value and Two-Digit Strategies
summary: A five-day sequence for counting to 120, composing tens and ones, comparing two-digit numbers, adding with place-value strategies, and finding ten more or less.

materials.name: Tens-and-ones mat
alternatives: two columns labeled tens and ones on paper

materials.name: Base-ten blocks
alternatives: bundles of ten sticks and single sticks
drawn tens rods and ones dots

days.title: Count, Read, and Bundle to 120
days.objective: I can count, read, and write numbers to 120 and show that one ten is ten ones.
adultSetup: Prepare a collection that can be grouped into bundles of ten plus singles.
Mark several missing numbers on the chart, including numbers greater than 100.
days.textRecommendation: Choose a counting or collection book that shows objects organized in groups rather than only isolated numerals.

directions: Count forward from a number other than one and stop at a named target.
Fill two missing numbers on the chart and explain the pattern.
Count ten single objects, bundle them, and state that one ten is the same quantity as ten ones.
Continue counting bundles and singles while matching the quantity to written numerals.
Model reading and writing a number greater than 100 without treating the chart as the counted quantity.
Build several quantities with bundles and singles and count them together.
Start at different numbers and count forward across a decade and across 100.
Match spoken number names, written numerals, and represented quantities.
Complete five on-screen count-to-120 and ten-as-ones checks.
Build one adult-named number with bundles and singles and write its numeral without copying.
Choose a starting number below 120, count forward ten numbers, and write the sequence.
Use one bundle and ten singles and pair each single with one stick in the bundle.
Count within a smaller range, then cross only one decade after the representation is secure.

masteryEvidence: Counts forward within 120 from at least two non-one starting numbers.
Represents and explains one ten as ten ones and matches a quantity to its written numeral.

days.title: Teens and Decade Numbers
days.objective: I can show teen numbers and decade numbers as tens and ones.
adultSetup: Prepare bundles of ten, single objects, and numeral cards for 10 through 19 and 20 through 90 by tens.
days.textRecommendation: Choose a counting book or visual collection that organizes quantities in rows or groups of ten.

directions: Trade ten singles for one bundle and explain why the quantity stays the same.
Count by tens to ninety using bundles.
Build fourteen as one ten and four ones, connecting each digit to its place.
Build forty as four tens and zero ones and contrast 14 with 40.
Read each number aloud after checking the model rather than relying on digit order alone.
Build and record several teen numbers.
Build and record several decade numbers with zero ones.
Sort numeral cards into teen numbers and decade numbers, then justify each placement with tens and ones.
Complete five on-screen ten-ones, teen-number, and decade-number checks.
Represent one teen number and one decade number and explain what each digit means.
Write a pair such as 16 and 60, draw each with tens and ones, and explain why the same digits have different values.
Contrast one teen number with one decade number using physical bundles.
Say tens and ones before writing each digit into its labeled column.

masteryEvidence: Represents a teen number as one ten and the correct number of ones.
Represents a decade number as the correct number of tens and zero ones.

days.title: Compare Two-Digit Numbers
days.objective: I can compare two two-digit numbers by looking at tens first and ones second.
adultSetup: Prepare base-ten materials, two tens-and-ones mats, numeral cards, and greater-than, less-than, and equals symbols.
Include comparison pairs with different tens, equal tens, and equal values.
days.textRecommendation: Choose a story or picture showing two collections and discuss how organization into tens makes comparison easier.

directions: Compare two single-digit quantities with more, less, or equal language.
Build two tens in two different ways and confirm both represent twenty.
Build 34 and 28 and compare the tens before the ones.
Build 34 and 37 and explain why the ones decide when the tens are equal.
Place the comparison symbol between numerals only after stating the relationship in words.
Build and compare three pairs of two-digit numbers.
For each pair, point to the first place that determines the comparison.
Include an equal pair represented with different-looking materials to separate quantity from arrangement.
Complete five on-screen tens-and-ones and comparison checks.
Build or draw one comparison and explain why the chosen symbol is true.
Order three two-digit numeral cards from least to greatest and justify both comparison steps.
Use pairs with clearly different tens and cover the ones column.
Pair tens rods one-to-one before naming more or less, then uncover ones only when tens match.

masteryEvidence: Compares two-digit numbers using tens and ones rather than an unrelated cue.
Uses greater than, less than, or equal language and matches it to the correct symbol.

days.title: Add with Tens and Ones
days.objective: I can add within 100 by combining tens and ones and explain when ten ones become a new ten.
adultSetup: Prepare base-ten materials and two tens-and-ones mats.
Choose examples that include adding a two-digit number and one-digit number, adding two two-digit numbers, and making a new ten.
days.textRecommendation: Choose a short joining story involving grouped objects, such as boxes of ten crayons plus single crayons.

directions: Build a two-digit number and state its tens and ones.
Add ten without recounting the ones and describe what changes.
Model 32 plus 5 by combining ones while keeping tens organized.
Model 38 plus 7, trade ten ones for one ten, and recount by place value.
Write an equation and explain that adding tens to tens and ones to ones preserves each unit's value.
Solve one example without composing a new ten and one example that does.
Connect the blocks to a drawing of tens and ones and then to an equation.
Estimate whether the result should be greater than the starting number and check the written answer against the model.
Complete six on-screen addition and ten-more-or-less checks.
Solve one adult-given addition problem with a model or drawing and explain the place-value steps.
Solve the same addition with blocks and a drawing, then explain how each part corresponds.
Use a two-digit number plus one or two ones without composing a ten.
Keep tens and ones in labeled columns, then introduce a trade only after separate-place addition is secure.

masteryEvidence: Adds within 100 using a concrete model or drawing aligned by place value.
Explains that ten ones can be composed into one ten when needed.

days.title: Ten More, Ten Less, and Subtract Tens
days.objective: I can find ten more or ten less and subtract groups of ten from a two-digit number.
adultSetup: Prepare the number chart, base-ten materials, and cards showing plus ten and minus ten.
Choose subtraction examples using multiples of ten whose answers stay at or above zero.
days.textRecommendation: Choose a short story about adding or removing full packages of ten while single items remain unchanged.

directions: Find a number on the chart, then move one row down and one row up.
Use bundles to explain why those moves change the number by ten.
Build 54, add one ten, and explain why the ones digit stays four.
Return to 54, remove one ten, and connect the model to ten less.
Model 70 minus 30 as seven tens minus three tens and check the result by adding thirty back.
Find ten more and ten less for numbers with and without zero ones.
Subtract multiples of ten with bundles, drawings, and equations.
Compare the starting number and answer and explain which place changed.
Complete six on-screen comparison, addition, ten-more-or-less, and subtract-tens checks.
Solve one subtract-tens example with a representation and verify it using addition.
Create a three-step chain using ten more or ten less and ask an adult to predict and verify the ending number.
Use only full bundles and subtract one bundle at a time while counting tens aloud.
Return to a two-digit number with unchanged ones and physically remove or add exactly one tens rod.

masteryEvidence: Finds ten more and ten less for varied two-digit numbers and explains the place-value change.
Subtracts multiples of ten from multiples of ten using a tens-based strategy.
Uses comparison or inverse addition to check whether a result is reasonable.

accommodationNotes: Read directions and story contexts aloud and allow replay without penalty.
Use tactile bundles, labeled place-value columns, and high-contrast numerals rather than color as the only grouping cue.
Accept object placement, pointing, eye gaze, drawing, signing, or spoken explanation when writing is not assessed.
Reduce the number range temporarily while preserving the same place-value relationship, then rebuild the range after success.

review.notes: Machine-validated instructional draft. It requires named human curriculum review before production use.
